correctness.rationale: On a fixed ordered axis, two nonnested comparison queries (a,b),(c,d) with a<=c and b<=d obey a preferred to b => c preferred to d by the no-valley property, so cannot be shattered. Strictly nested pairs can be deleted as consecutive endpoint blocks in independently chosen orders, leaving all comparisons outside the selected pairs identical: this produces a strong coordinate cube. Choosing 2k axis positions and pairing extremes gives exactly binom(n,2k) supports, hence VC=floor(n/2). The adaptive extreme-pair deletion tree has 2^(n-1) distinct consistent paths; the class has exactly that many strict orders, proving Ldim=n-1. A common peak at k+1/2 and explicit utility samples 8i±1 on nested pairs realize all 2^k continuous preference labels with strict monotonicity on each side; interpolation gives infinite VC for unrestricted qualitative continuous single-peaked utilities. Independent full pair-comparison trace enumeration confirmed the nested-support criterion for n<=5; finite checks support, not prove, the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The source provides the complete labeled comparison-shattering complex, fixed-complement cubes, exact VC and Littlestone dimension on every fixed-axis single-peaked ranking domain, plus a concrete common-peak infinite VC counterexample for unrestricted continuous one-peaked preferences. Classical endpoint-deletion enumeration, sign representation and elicitation complexity do not state the full binary-pair shattering support classification. The Basu–Echenique 2020 paper does explicitly give finite VC as an illustrative claim for qualitative real single-peaked preferences, but the current explicit counterexample shows that illustration does not apply as written to unrestricted utilities; it does not impugn their separate main expected-utility results.
residual_risks: Potential previously established nested-comparison support facets under social-choice elicitation or permutation-tope language.

value.rationale: Complete classification of shattered pair-comparison supports and strong cubes for a standard social-choice domain is a natural combinatorial invariant. The exact VC versus adaptive Ldim gap is meaningful for online preference learning, and the continuous common-peak construction identifies a sharp limitation of a widely cited qualitative finite-VC example. These are structural and conceptually motivated results, not a tiny enumeration.

residual_risks: The continuous witness applies only to unrestricted strictly unimodal utilities; symmetry, distance utility, Lipschitz slope, shared cardinal structure or parametric classes may restore finite VC.
